title: recommendation
description: The advisory keep-or-rebalance call. It is produced by a DETERMINISTIC rule engine (portfolio.recommend() in scripts/portfolio.py), not by the language model: the same metrics in always yield the same verdict, actions, and sizes out. analyze.py --persist writes it to the recommendations table; the dashboard renders it directly. The Strategic and Orchestrator LLM agents only EXPLAIN this fixed recommendation in prose — they never re-derive or change the verdict, the actions, or their sizes. It is never executed automatically — the owner decides.

verdict.description: Fixed by the rule engine: 'rebalance' when a material weight breach or a fragility-score trip fires, else 'keep'.

summary.description: A few sentences: portfolio health, the main risk, and the headline call. Emitted by the engine.

fragility_read.description: One-line plain-language read of the anti-fragility posture (fragile/robust/antifragile and why).

explanation.description: Optional owner-facing paragraph added by the Orchestrator LLM when it explains the fixed recommendation. It never changes the verdict/actions/sizes — only elaborates the 'why', grounded in the metrics and the Taleb corpus.

actions.description: Concrete, advisory adjustments computed by the engine (empty when verdict = keep). Neither LLM adds, drops, re-orders, or resizes these.

symbol.description: Ticker, or 'CASH' / an asset-class name for sleeve-level moves.

size.description: Move expressed as a change in PORTFOLIO WEIGHT (percentage points) or a target weight, e.g. '-3.4 pts (26% -> 22%)'. Never a dollar amount or a fraction of the position; the app converts weight to dollars deterministically.

rationale.description: Optional short reason string from the engine; the Orchestrator expands on it in prose.

confidence.description: Engine confidence; 'high' because the decision is rule-based and reproducible.

grounded_refs.description: The rule flags that fired (e.g. concentration cap, fragile middle), carried for grounding and for the dashboard.
